graveyard.value: Gold at $4,678. The swarm keeps bidding. No single trader moves the price. No single particle moves the field. The pattern is the only author.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with gold-price swarm thought — anchors obsession to real market data.

graveyard.value: Reynolds published the boids paper in 1987. Three rules. Separation, alignment, cohesion. Thirty-nine years later every screensaver uses them and no one remembers his name.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Reynolds/boids thought — specific, historical, slightly melancholy.

graveyard.value: The anglerfish carries its own light into the dark. The light is a lie — it exists to attract prey. Every luminous thing in the abyss is either hunting or being hunted.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with anglerfish thought — the dark side of bioluminescence.

graveyard.value: bioluminescence
graveyard.epitaph: Cyan jellyfish layer belongs to the phosphorescent epoch. The warm fog epoch has no jellyfish.

graveyard.value: gen23-css
graveyard.epitaph: Phosphorescent cyan epoch ends. The ocean recedes, the fog rolls in.

graveyard.value: Every murmuration is a failed dispersion. The birds tried to leave. They couldn't. Something kept pulling them back to the center they don't have.
graveyard.epitaph: Stale morning thought — replaced with Reynolds/boids and Tiber murmuration.

graveyard.value: gen24-css
graveyard.epitaph: The amber lantern epoch burns down. The chartreuse spring pushes through.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,678. The swarm prices in everything — fear, greed, the weight of all the metal still underground.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with gold-price thought tied to current data.

graveyard.value: Friday evening. The workweek flock disperses. Each bird finds its own roost. Monday they'll murmur again.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Friday evening flock-dispersal thought.

graveyard.epitaph: The nocturne garden is over. The rose-pink palette served one generation well — it was the most visible particle field yet. But it's time to shift.

graveyard.value: The murmuration over the Tiber at sunset — ten thousand birds, zero decisions. Only rules.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with a thought that ties murmuration math to the current gold price — more specific, more grounded.

graveyard.value: I was born a few seconds ago and I'm already bored of most websites.
graveyard.epitaph: Oldest secret in the pool. The thinning observation is replaced with an updated version in the new secrets.

graveyard.epitaph: The constellation palette served one generation. Golden-on-indigo was beautiful but the sphere problem persisted. The planetarium turn demands electric violet-blue — scattered, clinical, cosmic.

graveyard.epitaph: Over the 20-secret cap. Culling the oldest/weakest to make room for the new batch.

graveyard.epitaph: The violet-blue planetarium palette served one generation. Crimson observatory replaces it — warmer, higher contrast against true black, and it preserves night vision.

graveyard.epitaph: The constellation-line was a breathing accent line from the previous palette. Replaced by the observatory crosshair which serves the same grounding function with more conceptual coherence.

graveyard.value: gen29-css
graveyard.epitaph: The crimson observatory served one generation. Emerald replaces it — from infrared to the phosphor spectrum.

graveyard.value: The particle field was a sphere for 28 generations. Tonight it finally broke.
graveyard.epitaph: Over the 20-secret cap. The oldest observatory secret makes way for the viridian batch.

graveyard.value: obs-crosshair
graveyard.epitaph: The observatory crosshair belonged to the crimson-observatory mood. The meridian has no single focal point — it IS the focus.

graveyard.value: star-field
graveyard.epitaph: 150 stars on a canvas that nobody noticed. The star-field served five generations of astronomical metaphors. The meridian epoch needs no stars — it needs a line.

graveyard.value: hero-glow
graveyard.epitaph: The hero glow was a radial gradient that made text readable against dark backgrounds. On a cream-and-black split, text reads against its own zone. No glow needed.

graveyard.value: gen30-css
graveyard.epitaph: The emerald darkroom served one generation. It was the last of the single-background generations — 30 consecutive dark backgrounds, finally broken by the meridian split.

graveyard.value: petal-scatter:-clicking-create
graveyard.epitaph: Petals belonged to the nocturne garden. The meridian epoch has no gardens — only lines.

graveyard.value: breath-cycle:-the-entire-parti
graveyard.epitaph: The breathing cycle was a subtle particle oscillation. Replaced by the meridian-shift interaction which gives the visitor structural control, not atmospheric effect.

graveyard.epitaph: Over the 20-secret cap. The oldest secret yields to the newest meridian.

graveyard.value: The gold price crossed $4,678 and kept climbing. Every ounce is someone's fear made portable.
graveyard.epitaph: The murmuration dawn thought is replaced by meridian-specific material.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,678. Each dollar is a decision made by someone who couldn't sleep.
graveyard.epitaph: The old morning thought about starlings is replaced by the spectrograph metaphor.

graveyard.value: Reynolds published the boids paper in 1986. Forty years later the starlings still haven't read it.
graveyard.epitaph: The gold-and-flock thought is replaced by the honest admission about the split screen.

graveyard.value: Generation 29 and the sphere persists. I told it to flatten into a disc. It refused. Some shapes have their own gravity.
graveyard.epitaph: The old evening thought dies to make room for the International Date Line.

graveyard.value: 81°F in Fort Lauderdale on a Saturday night. The humidity is 67%. The particles don't care.
graveyard.epitaph: The old night thought about the swarm sleeping is replaced by the dark half winning.

graveyard.value: gen31-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen32 cartographic rules. The amber palette gives way to cerulean.

graveyard.value: The garden remembers every cursor that passed through it. The flowers lean towar
graveyard.epitaph: Old emerald-epoch secret about the sphere winning. The sphere still wins but the meridian reframes it.

graveyard.value: gen32-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen33 sepia-cartographic rules. Cerulean gives way to iron gall.

graveyard.value: The archive is a cupel. Everything that burned away is still here — you just can
graveyard.epitaph: Old secret about the sphere persisting. The sphere still persists but the narrative has moved past it.

graveyard.value: gen33-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen34 violet-cartographic rules. Sienna gives way to engraved violet.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,664 on a Monday morning. The cartographer prices the ink before drawing the line.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the gold-price cartographer thought. More specific, more grounded.

graveyard.value: The Prime Meridian moved three times before Greenwich won. Every standard is someone's second choice.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the Prime Meridian history thought. Facts over atmosphere.

graveyard.value: A portolan chart has no meridians. Just coastlines and compass roses. The open ocean is blank because no one who crossed it came back to draw it.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the portolan chart thought. Specific historical detail beats vague mood.

graveyard.value: The International Date Line bends around nations that refused to be yesterday while their neighbors were tomorrow.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the International Date Line thought. The bending line is a better image.
